name: Phosphate Transport (Pst System)
description: The Pst (phosphate-specific transport) system is a high-affinity ABC transporter that imports inorganic phosphate under limiting conditions. The system consists of PstS (periplasmic binding protein), PstA/PstC (membrane permeases), and PstB (ATP-binding protein). The Pst system is part of the Pho regulon regulated by PhoB/PhoR two-component system. Under phosphate limitation, PhoR activates PhoB which induces pst genes and other phosphate scavenging systems. The Pst system has nanomolar affinity for phosphate compared to the low-affinity Pit system. Mutations in pst cause constitutive Pho regulon expression.
scientificAccuracy: Based on structural and biochemical studies of the Pst ABC transporter and Pho regulon regulation.
